nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What methodology was used to evaluate the environmental impact of the antibacterial biocomposite?
nodes.answer: A life cycle assessment (LCA) based on ISO 14040 and 14044 was used to evaluate the environmental impact.
nodes.paragraph: To further enhance antibacterial proper - ties and sustainability performance, a novel biocomposite based on PLA with hemp hurd filled with silver nanoparticles (AgNP) was developed. Here we present a life cycle assessment (LCA) based on ISO 14040 and 14044 to evaluate the added value of the antibacterial biocomposite compared to conventional antibacterial materials from an environmental perspective. The environmental impacts are analyzed in comparison to virgin PLA, fossil-based polypropylene (PP) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) combined in a disinfecting wipes and sterilized application. Our results show that the novel biocomposite has in general higher environmental impacts than its counterparts. Notably, our findings suggest a significant impact derived from high energy demand required for AgNP synthesis. To be able to compete with other materials, the energy demand needs to be minimized, which should be the focus of further research. nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What gap does this research aim to close regarding the AgNP-HH-PLA biocomposite?
nodes.answer: The research aims to close the gap regarding the lack of available life cycle assessment (LCA) for the AgNP-HH-PLA biocomposite.
nodes.paragraph: We endeavor to bridge the data in the sustainability by assessing the environmental impact of this PLA-based antibacterial biocomposite. We compare the antibacterial material with a non-antibacterial control and perform a life cycle assessment (LCA) based on ISO 14040 [ 7] and ISO 14044 [ 8]. Based on the results, we infer the possible directions for further development of the AgNP-HH-PLA biocomposite. While the technology and its development on how to pro - duce the novel biocomposite has been developed by Khan et al., 2016 [ 9], this study focuses on the environmental impact of the newly developed material. While the environmental assessment of nanocomposites as well as connected antibac - terial properties has been conducted before [ 10, 11], cur - rently no LCA for AgNP-HH-PLA is available, thereby this research is closing a gap with regards to the environmen - tal impact of the novel biocomposite also in comparison to other fossil-based and bio-based alternatives. There are different ways to obtain antibacterial activity which also result in different degrees of hygiene. To reduce the microbial load on objects or the skin and mucous mem - brane, one can choose between disinfection or sterilization.

nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What does the Dutch Life Cycle Assessments (Lucas) food database quantify?
nodes.answer: The Dutch Lucas quantify all inputs and materials used through the entire product life cycle, including processing, transport, distribution, and waste. The Lucas were performed following the ISO 14,040 and 14,044 guidelines, with an attributional approach and hierarchical perspective.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of assessing the environmental impact of the textile supply chain using life cycle assessment methodology?
nodes.answer: The significance lies in understanding the environmental implications of the entire textile supply chain processes from raw material extraction to end-of-life disposal, helping to identify areas for improvement and sustainability measures.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does each life cycle assessment (LCA) stage of UPF production contribute to the negative environmental impact?
nodes.answer: Each stage of UPF production contributes differently to the negative environmental impact, characterized by monoculture crops, high energy demands, long transport chains, and excessive packaging.
